newsitem.title: UK: Conoco gets OK to develop Banff N.Sea field.
newsitem.headline: Conoco gets OK to develop Banff N.Sea field.

text.p: U.S. company Conoco said on Wednesday it had been granted approval to develop the U.K. North Sea Banff oilfield following a successful six-month production test.

Conoco, a subsidiary of DuPont, owns 31.7 percent of Banff. The other equity partners are Enterprise Oil (27.9 percent), Ranger Oil (26.2 percent), Hardy Exploration and Production (12.4 percent) and Santos Europe (1.8 percent).
Banff, which lies 200 kilometres east of Aberdeen in block 29/2a, has been producing at a rate of 35,000 barrels of oil per day (bpd) since September via two development wells.
Conoco said the results of the extended well test "proved the reservoir's potential for further development".
The field has recoverable reserves of about 60 million barrels of oil and some 39 billion cubic feet of associated gas.
"Additional potential exists in other areas of the field which could result in further development," Conoco said in a statement.
